title: Special relativity can warp chemical bonds – now we've seen it happen
description: An experiment with a charged molecule of bismuth and carbon reveals how effects from Albert Einstein’s special relativity reshape the standard understanding of chemical bonds
author: Karmela Padavic-Callaghan

title: Resuscitated human retinas respond to light 10 hours after death
description: Perfusing donor human retinas with blood and oxygen meant they continued to respond to light for up to 10 hours after death, marking a significant step towards eye transplants that restore vision
author: Helen Thomson

title: Mathematics of thermodynamics is being rewritten after 200 years
description: The laws of physics that concern heat and work could gain a firmer mathematical footing thanks to “gauge theory”, which already helps us understand quantum fields
author: Karmela Padavic-Callaghan

title: Injection halves risk of chromosome error common in older human eggs
description: Egg cells missing a key protein may be more likely to end up with the wrong number of chromosomes, but an mRNA injection that helps the cells make the protein reduces the problem
author: Carissa Wong

title: A worm that lived half a billion years ago preferred turning right
description: Fossils of Spriggina floundersi provide the earliest evidence of animals favouring one side of the body over the other – a feature of nervous systems that we see in our own right- and left-handedness
author: James Woodford

title: Seeding clouds with seawater could prevent a super El Niño
description: A modelling study suggests marine cloud brightening could shade the eastern Pacific and reduce a global temperature spike from El Niño, but there could be unexpected consequences
author: Alec Luhn
